dana: Quick RFC follow-up: attribute-claim tokens vs compact role-id API keys for svc->svc. Need perf, audit, and migration tradeoffs.

akshay: I prefer attribute-first for expressivity, but worried about per-request policy eval cost.

sam: Cacheability is the big ops concern. CDNs/gateways like fixed role ids. Attributes need canonicalization to work.

lee: Idea: issuer emits an optional policy-hash + short role-id derived from canonical claims. Gateway fast-path uses role-id hash; fallback to full eval.

marie: Migration plan: mint attribute tokens gradually, attach derived role-ids for high-throughput routes, and phase out old keys after 60d.

akshay: Example claim set: {org:redwood,proj:payments,svc:billing,caps:[infer:invoke]}. Standardize names and serialization.

dana: Pros/cons captured: attributes = flexible, fine-grained audit, easier revocation via policy; role-id = simple, cache-friendly, lower latency. Hybrid seems best.

lee: SRE: run perf bench? @infra-bot please run small eval.

infra-bot: run:policy-eval-bench --paths=50k --concurrency=200 -> p50=0.9ms p95=6.5ms cache-hit p95=1.1ms

marie: Numbers look acceptable for internal services. External low-latency endpoints should keep role-id fast path.

sam: Add telemetry: tag auth.eval.path=role|attr to measure fallback rate.

dana: Rollout steps: 1) claim schema RFC update; 2) issuer derive policy-hash+role-id; 3) gateway fast/fallback path; 4) canary 2 weeks; 5) monitor telemetry and iterate.

marie: I'll post RFC diff EOD.

dana: Thanks — will schedule a 30m sync if RFC gets +1s.
